Mary Peltola Names Former Obama White House and Interior Official Raina Thiele as Chief of Staff

Dena’ina Athabascan and Yup’ik Alaskan brings nearly two decades of federal policy experience to Peltola’s incoming U.S. Senate office.
by Levi Rickert November 24, 2026November 24, 2026

Overview:

Senator-elect Mary Peltola has named Alaska Native Raina Thiele, a former Obama White House official and senior advisor at the Department of the Interior, as chief of staff for her incoming U.S. Senate office.

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:05
Instaread

Senator-elect Mary Peltola (D-AK) has named Raina Thiele, a former White House and U.S. Department of the Interior official, as her chief of staff as she begins assembling her incoming U.S. Senate office.

Thiele, an Alaska Native with Dena’ina Athabascan and Yup’ik heritage, brings nearly two decades of federal policy experience, including service in the administrations of Presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden. She most recently served as a senior advisor to Peltola’s Senate campaign.

“Putting Alaska first starts with ensuring we have a seat at the table where decisions are being made, and Raina Thiele has dedicated her career to ensuring Alaska voices are heard in the halls of power,” Peltola said.

Peltola pointed to Thiele’s experience working in two presidential administrations and her background addressing Alaska issues at the federal level as important qualifications for leading her Senate staff.

White House experience included tribal affairs portfolio

During the Obama administration, Thiele served for nearly five years in the White House Office of Management and Budget, first as a legislative analyst and later as a program examiner, working on domestic and international policy issues, including energy and tribal legislation.

She subsequently became Associate Director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs and Public Engagement, where she served as President Obama’s liaison to tribal governments and the American Indian and Alaska Native community.

In that position, Thiele worked on issues affecting tribal nations, including climate change, Arctic policy and energy. She also played a leading role in organizing Obama’s historic 2015 trip to Alaska, which brought national attention to Alaska Native communities and the effects of climate change in the state.

Following her White House service, Thiele continued working on federal policy matters before joining the Biden administration in 2021. She served as Senior Advisor for Alaska Affairs and Strategic Priorities at the Department of the Interior from 2021 to 2025. In that role, she focused on federal priorities affecting Alaska. U.S. Department of the Interior.

“I’m honored to have this opportunity to continue serving my home state in a new capacity,” Thiele said. “Senator-elect Peltola has always put Alaska first, and I look forward to helping her build a Senate office that reflects that commitment and delivers for Alaskans across the state.”

Born and raised in Alaska, Thiele is Dena’ina Athabascan, Yup’ik and German. Her family traces its roots to Pedro Bay Village on Lake Iliamna and Alexander Creek near Mount Susitna.

She graduated from Yale College and earned a Master of Public Policy degree from Harvard Kennedy School of Government.

Thiele’s appointment places an Alaska Native with experience in White House tribal affairs and federal policymaking at the center of Peltola’s incoming Senate operation.

She is married to Charlie Galbraith (Navajo), who previously served in the White House for President Barack Obama as Associate Director of Intergovernmental Affairs and Public Engagement.
